issues.failure_explanation: From the residual inequality, integrating dV_hat/dt gives \hat{V}(x(T)) - \hat{V}(x(0)) >= -J_T - \epsilon T. Multiplying by -1 reverses the inequality, yielding J_T >= \hat{V}(x(0)) - \hat{V}(x(T)) - \epsilon T. The proof instead asserts J_T <= \hat{V}(x(0)) - \hat{V}(x(T)) + \epsilon T. This sign error inverts the direction of the bound, falsely deducing an upper bound on J(x_0; \hat{u}) and on \hat{V} - V^* from a subsolution inequality. Furthermore, the lower bound 0 <= \hat{V}(x) - V^*(x) is asserted without proof by confusing the approximate value function with the suboptimal policy cost; an HJB subsolution actually satisfies \hat{V} <= V^*.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a supersolution condition R(x) <= \epsilon to obtain upper bounds on policy cost and suboptimality, which is nonconvex and outside the paper's convex LMI formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The suboptimality guarantee for \hat{V} (Theorem 3.6) and the performance guarantee on the feedback control J(x_0; \hat{u}) - V^*(x_0) <= \epsilon T(x_0) (Corollary 3.7) are invalidated.
issues.title: Inequality reversal in suboptimality bound proof
issues.why_classification: The paper's core theoretical optimality guarantees are lost; subsolutions from the convex LMI can only certify lower bounds on cost, so establishing suboptimality upper bounds requires an essentially different, nonconvex framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For $V^* \in H^s(\Omega) \cap \mathcal{H}_\kappa$, the best approximation from $\mathcal{H}_M = \text{span}\{\kappa(\cdot, x_i)\}_{i=1}^M$ satisfies:
\[
\|V^* - \hat{V}\|_{\mathcal{H}_\kappa} = O(h^s)
\]
when the centers form a quasi-uniform grid with fill distance $h$ (see \cite{wendland_scattered}).

issues.failure_explanation: A Gaussian RKHS consists solely of real-analytic functions and is not norm-equivalent to any Sobolev space H^s(\Omega). A general function V^* in H^s(\Omega) does not belong to the Gaussian RKHS, making ||V^* - \hat{V}||_{\mathcal{H}_\kappa} undefined. Furthermore, in scattered data approximation, native space norm errors do not decay algebraically as O(h^s); algebraic rates O(h^s) apply in L_2 for finitely smooth kernels (such as Matérn or Wendland kernels), whereas Gaussian kernels provide spectral convergence for functions strictly in their native space.

failure_location.quote: The Gaussian kernel generates an RKHS $\mathcal{H}_\kappa$ that is norm-equivalent to certain Sobolev spaces. Specifically, for the Gaussian kernel on bounded domains, $\mathcal{H}_\kappa$ embeds continuously into $H^s(\Omega)$ for all $s \geq 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Theorem 3.12 for a finitely smooth kernel (e.g., Matérn or Wendland kernel) whose RKHS is norm-equivalent to H^s(\Omega), for which standard scattered data approximation theory yields ||\nabla V^* - \nabla \hat{V}||_{L^2(\Omega)} = O(h^{s-1}).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.12 fails as stated and proved for Gaussian kernels approximating H^s functions.
issues.title: False Sobolev norm-equivalence and native space error bounds for Gaussian RKHS
issues.why_classification: The advertised algebraic convergence rate O(h^{s-1}) = O(M^{-(s-1)/n}) is preserved by replacing the Gaussian kernel with a standard Sobolev/Wendland kernel of appropriate smoothness.
